reference.title: Barbell Hack Squat
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Big breath in and brace at the top, hold it on the way down and through the bottom, breathe out as you pass the hardest part of the rise or at the top.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, a short pause, about 1.2 s up

prescription.progression: Add 2.5-5 kg when all sets reach the top of the rep range.

cues.text: Stand tall with the bar behind the legs, hands just outside the hips with an overhand grip, arms straight, shoulders back and chest up. Feet about hip width, toes slightly out.
Big breath, brace, then bend the knees forward and sit straight down, trunk nearly upright; let the bar slide down the backs of the thighs with straight arms.
Stop with the bar just behind the backs of the knees and the heels flat; no bounce.
Drive up through the whole foot, keeping the chest up and the bar close to the legs; breathe out past the hardest part.
Stand tall, squeeze the shoulder blades, breathe and brace for the next rep.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the arms or pulling with them
mistakes.fix: Arms are hooks: keep them straight and let the legs do the work.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning forward so it becomes a deadlift
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest up and push the knees forward; the trunk stays nearly upright.

mistakes.mistake: Bar catching on the hamstrings or calves
mistakes.fix: Keep the bar just off the legs and the knees moving forward.
Keep the whole foot down; a small plate under the heels is common for this lift.
Squeeze the shoulder blades back before each rep.

kinematics.norm: About hip width, toes slightly out (Lorenzetti 2018)
To about 90-110 degrees; the bar behind the legs limits depth (clinical opinion; Straub 2024)
Moderate: the knees travel forward and the trunk stays fairly upright (clinical opinion)
Fairly upright, like a front squat, since the load hangs close to the body's centre of mass (clinical opinion; Gullett 2009 for the front-loaded comparison)
Held behind the legs on straight arms, close to the backs of the thighs (common coaching)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Hack Squat, video (movement reference only)
Straub and Powers 2024, a biomechanical review of the squat exercise: implications for clinical practice (Int J Sports Phys Ther)
Lorenzetti et al. 2018, how to squat: stance widths, foot angles and experience (BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil)
Gullett, Tillman, Gutierrez & Chow 2009, a biomechanical comparison of back and front squats in healthy trained individuals (J Strength Cond Res 23(1):284-292; PubMed 19002072)

cautions: Start the bar from a rack or blocks at hand height behind you, or deadlift it from the floor behind the heels with good form.
Knee pain: the knees travel far forward in this lift; reduce depth or skip it.
Keep the back flat and the shoulders back.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Heels up on a small plate to allow an upright trunk with limited ankle mobility.
Straps help if grip fails before the legs.
regressions: Dumbbell squat with the weights at the sides.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Main movers: the forward knees and upright trunk put most of the work on the knee extensors (Straub 2024).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Main movers: the forward knees and upright trunk put most of the work on the knee extensors (Straub 2024).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Extends the hip out of the bottom.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Extends the hip out of the bottom.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Control the forward travel of the knees.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Control the forward travel of the knees.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the back flat with the load hanging from the shoulders.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the back flat with the load hanging from the shoulders.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the knees tracking over the feet.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the knees tracking over the feet.

muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulders up against the hanging bar.

muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Holds the arms slightly behind the body.

muscleNotes.lats_l: Keep the straight arms close to the body.
